title: RFID Integration
description: Identify, test and integrate an RFID reader without changing production configuration.
requirements: Access to the host without altering production configuration

nodes.title: Protect the production system
nodes.body: Do not change reader, controller, credential or production settings until the system and rollback path are known.

nodes.title: Which RFID reader looks like yours?
nodes.body: Check the label for manufacturer and exact model. Choose Other if uncertain.

outcomes.label: None of these / I don’t know

nodes.title: Record visual identifiers
nodes.body: Photograph the front, rear, connectors and label. Record manufacturer, model and serial number without unplugging production equipment.

nodes.title: Trace the cable safely
nodes.body: Follow the cable visually. Do not disconnect it. USB ends at a host; Ethernet usually ends at a switch; reader wiring may end at a controller.

nodes.title: Test the reader in a plain text editor
nodes.body: Open Notepad or another plain text field, focus it, then present a known card.

nodes.title: USB Keyboard Wedge confirmed
nodes.body: The reader behaves as a keyboard. Capture the emitted value in the target field. It may be formatted credential data, CSN or another configured value—not necessarily the physical UID.

nodes.title: Check layout and reader formatting
nodes.body: Compare OS keyboard layout with reader configuration and inspect prefixes, suffixes, decimal/hex conversion and bit order. Avoid production changes until configuration is backed up.

nodes.title: Compare card technologies
nodes.body: Record which credentials work. The reader frequency and protocol must support the card; enrollment or keys may also be required.

nodes.title: Check USB enumeration
nodes.body: Windows: open Device Manager and inspect Smart card readers, Keyboards and unknown devices. Try a known-good port/cable only if safe.

nodes.title: Install the correct signed driver
nodes.body: Use the exact manufacturer/model driver and verify OS compatibility. Do not use untrusted driver sites.

nodes.title: Verify power, port and cable
nodes.body: Check LEDs, a known-good USB port and approved cable. If still absent, test the reader on a non-production host or replace it.

nodes.title: Likely USB or reader hardware fault
nodes.body: Document tests and replace with an approved compatible unit. Preserve the original configuration.

nodes.title: Check PC/SC reader and card detection
nodes.body: Confirm the PC/SC service is running, the reader is listed, then present a known compatible card.

nodes.title: Use direct PC/SC integration
nodes.body: Integrate through the OS PC/SC API/SDK and handle card events. If the model supports Keyboard Wedge, it may be configured only after backing up settings and confirming production impact.

nodes.title: Inspect vendor configuration
nodes.body: Export or screenshot current settings first. Check output encoding and credential format using the official vendor utility.

nodes.title: Verify Ethernet and PoE
nodes.body: Check link LEDs, approved PoE source, switch port/VLAN and the documented IP. Do not factory-reset or move production ports.

nodes.title: Test IP connectivity
nodes.expectedResult: Replies with stable latency. On Windows use: ping <READER_IP>

nodes.title: Check the network path
nodes.body: Confirm local subnet, gateway, VLAN, switch port and firewall with the network owner. ICMP may be disabled, so verify using the documented service port.

nodes.title: How does the reader expose events?
nodes.body: Consult official model documentation. Common integrations include HTTP API/webhooks, raw TCP, MQTT or a vendor SDK.

nodes.title: Integrate using the documented network interface
nodes.body: Use test credentials and a non-production endpoint first. Authenticate, validate payloads, handle retries and never assume the returned credential field is the physical UID.

nodes.title: Identify the access controller
nodes.body: Record controller manufacturer/model and reader wiring (for example Wiegand or OSDP) visually. Events usually come from the controller API/SDK, not directly from the reader.

nodes.title: Find the system owner and official interface
nodes.body: Locate controller/VMS/access-control documentation and the responsible owner. Determine IP, API/SDK and a safe test environment before changes.

nodes.title: RFID quick reference
nodes.body: 125 kHz commonly covers low-frequency proximity credentials. 13.56 MHz covers NFC, MIFARE, MIFARE DESFire and ISO 14443 A/B. UID/CSN identifies a chip, while credential data may be transformed, secured or stored in an application. Never assume displayed output equals the physical UID.
